Subject: Post-call: Greystone deployment modes & networking asks

Thanks again for the call earlier today — good conversation. Quick recap from our side and a few asks so our netops/security teams can evaluate: 

Recap
- We're evaluating three hosting options for inference: Hosted API (fastest), Dedicated reserved capacity, and Private VPC/on-prem.
- Internally we're leaning toward Private VPC for data residency and flow control, but want to confirm network patterns and operational impacts before committing.

Primary asks
1) PrivateLink vs VPC Peering: pros/cons for latency, egress behavior, and whether we need to open outbound allowlists from our side.
2) Egress IPs: do you require allowlisting of any static Redwood egress IPs for callbacks or telemetry?
3) Inbound connections: can Redwood accept inbound connections (service initiated from your side) or must all calls originate from our VPC?
4) TLS/mTLS: how is cert management handled for private deployments?
5) Can you share a simple network diagram + one-pager comparing the two connectivity modes and an estimated SOW/quote range for Private VPC?

Attached: greystone-infra-reqs.pdf (internal requirements doc) — Samir (netops) will chime in shortly with more technical items.

Next step: is a 60-min technical deep-dive with our netops + security next week feasible? Prefer Wed/Thu mornings PT.

Thanks,

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Post-call: Greystone deployment modes & networking asks

Thanks Ellen — great to meet you and Samir on the call. I pulled together a compact set of answers and a couple of artifacts to help your netops team evaluate. Attaching: redwood-privatelink-vs-peering-onepager.pdf and a sample-network-diagram.png.

Quick answers up front:
- PrivateLink (interface endpoints): typically simplest for customers who want per-tenant private connectivity without route table changes. Traffic originates from your VPC to the interface endpoint; we do not require you to open outbound internet egress for normal inference traffic.
- VPC Peering (route-based): supports lower-level routing between VPCs and can be simpler if you already peer many services, but requires route table updates and careful CIDR planning.
- Egress IPs: for Private VPC most inference traffic will stay inside the private connectivity path. There are a small set of control/management callbacks (agent health, billing telemetry) that may originate from Redwood-managed addresses; we will provide those CIDR ranges for allowlisting if needed.
- Inbound connections: Redwood does not require the customer to accept unsolicited inbound connections into their VPC. If you opt for an architecture where Redwood initiates connections (rare), we will document the ports/IPs and TLS requirements.
- TLS/mTLS: we support TLS termination on our side; for Private VPC deployments we can enable mTLS using customer-provided certs (recommended for finance/healthcare). Certificate rotation is supported via our ops portal or via customer KMS integration for on-prem/private installs.

Next steps I propose:
1) Technical deep-dive (45–60m) with Samir + netops: we can walk the sample diagram and map to your CIDRs. Please pick a slot here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2bGreystone-Network-Intake (I added a short intake form in the folder).
2) We will share a preliminary SOW range for Private VPC after the deep-dive and a short security package (SOC2 attestation + penetration test summary) if required.
3) If you want a tighter cost/latency estimate we can run a small dedicated benchmark on a mirrored workload (requires NDA).

I've looped in Marissa (solutions lead) and Ben (networks PM) to own the SOW and ops checklist.

-Jonas

Samir / Ellen — great questions. Below are the concrete answers and a proposed agenda for the deep-dive. I've attached a short ops checklist (privatenet-ops-checklist.docx) we use for Private VPC onboarding.

Concrete answers
- Egress CIDRs (control/management): 34.201.128.0/20, 52.23.64.0/20, 18.205.0.0/18. These are the IP ranges used for management callbacks and telemetry in our US region. If you need them in CIDR blocks to add to NAT rules or firewall allowlists, use the three above. (Note: the inference traffic over PrivateLink stays within the private connectivity path and does not traverse these egress addresses.)
- Ports/protocols: control plane uses HTTPS (TCP 443) for all callbacks and telemetry. Optional metrics ingestion uses TLS over 443 or a dedicated port if you prefer (we can finalize in the deep-dive).
- Inbound routes: not required for standard PrivateLink flows — your VPC initiates the connection to the interface endpoint and Redwoods' service side responds over that connection. No unsolicited inbound route setup needed.
- Session affinity: our PrivateLink front door includes a sticky-session layer per endpoint; multi-AZ routing is handled by the endpoint service and our backend autoplace. We will document expected connection TTLs and KV-cache behavior for LLMs in the deep-dive.
- Backup/data egress: customer-initiated peered connections for SFTP/backups are supported; if you want Redwood to pull backups from your S3 over a peering link, we'll list required VPC endpoints and S3 IAM roles in the SOW.
- mTLS: supported. We can accept customer certs and configure mutual TLS for the control plane. For inference traffic we typically rely on TLS; if you require mTLS we will enable it and coordinate cert rotation windows.

Proposed deep-dive agenda (45–60m)
1) Introductions + goals (5m)
2) Walk sample network diagram and map Greystone CIDRs to endpoints (15–20m)
3) Review egress/IP allowlist needs and control-plane flows (10–15m)
4) Discuss SOW scope for Private VPC (ports, SLAs, onboarding timeline) (10m)
5) Next steps + owners (5m)

Available slot confirmed: Thu 10/22 10:30–11:30 PT — we've penciled that in. If that works for you Samir, I'll send a calendar invite and include a short pre-call checklist to collect the final CIDRs.
